headline: Crude tops $95 on more tanker threats; grain holds steady
lead: WTI crude is at $95.36 overnight, up 1.3%, after Iran told Reuters its forces plan to intensify strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. Corn and wheat drifted lower overnight while beans firmed to $12.90½. Diesel costs for fall fieldwork are the thing to watch, not the grain board.
teaser: Crude pushes toward $95 on fresh Iran tanker threats while corn and beans sit quiet.

one_number.context: EPA wants to reallocate all of 2025's exempted biofuel volumes back into the mandate, a win for corn-based ethanol demand if it holds.

sections.title: Corn and wheat drift, beans firm
sections.body:
- Corn is at $4.81½ overnight, down 1¼ cents from Tuesday's $4.82¾ settle, still digesting last week's WASDE.
- Chicago wheat slipped 3 cents to $6.66¼ while soybeans gained 6¾ cents to $12.90½.
- CME says corn futures set a daily volume record, a sign of how much trade has moved through this market since Friday's report.
sections.so_what: Beans are the one leg of the complex still finding buyers this week.

sections.title: Crude pushes toward $95 on Hormuz threats
sections.body:
- WTI is at $95.36 overnight, up 1.3% from Tuesday's $94.14, after Iran signaled new tactics for tanker strikes in the Strait of Hormuz.
- This is the same Iran-Hormuz cycle that flared in July, cooled through August, and is now showing signs of life again.
sections.so_what: Diesel costs for fall fieldwork move with this, not with the grain board.

outside_the_pit.title: EPA proposes reallocating a year's worth of waived biofuel volumes
outside_the_pit.body: EPA wants to put 770 million RINs worth of 2025 exempted volumes back into the Renewable Fuel Standard, a potential lift for corn demand.

watch_list.desc: Weekly export sales; soybean bookings tied to China's purchase pace are the number to watch.
WTI above $95 for more than a couple sessions would say the Hormuz premium is building again, not fading.
Corn back under $4.80 would confirm harvest supply, not the WASDE bounce, is setting the tone.

source_summary: CME/CBOT overnight quotes, USDA, EPA, Reuters, AgWeb, Drovers, Feedstuffs, OilPrice.com

lines: Corn harvest price so far: $4.95 vs $4.62 projected (+7.1%), 9 of 22 trading days in.
Soybeans harvest price so far: $12.88 vs $11.09 projected (+16.1%), 9 of 22 trading days in.
harvest_clock.note: Average of the daily CBOT settles through Oct 13, figured the way USDA RMA does. RMA posts corn at $4.96. RMA posts soybeans at $12.89. Window and projected price: USDA RMA, as of Oct 13. Oct 1-31 window, most states.
